conclusion: This frozen image was not itself run. The firmware start runs in the firmware-stop, first-job and job-session images, which passed on port 3-1 (first job: start result=0 step=29 count=29 waited_us=669 memory=2).
narrative: Image behavior: before any power change it prepares the firmware (code, data and the 16 KiB MIPS page table in write-back image RAM; the nineteen shared resources in the first 45 pages of the Normal-NC block at 0x41c00000, zeroed; system init and runtime configuration carry the 1,008 MHz core clock; queues formatted; the 29-step plan built; a refusal ends the run before the ON). It powers the GPU on to CORE6 status 8 within 200 ms, checks the wrapper, SMC0 and three GPU register pages as identity Device-nGnRnE mappings, reads the identity (36.56.104.183), drm_ctrl and SMC0 +0xb0. It starts only while the 1 s start bound and a 100 ms report fit before the 1.5 s session deadline, which also keeps the start's end 500 ms before the monitor's 2 s recovery; otherwise status 7. It reads RGX_CR_TIMER and writes one timer-correlation record into slot 1, sequence 1; writes SMC0 +0xb0 = 2 and drm_ctrl = 0 and records both read-backs without writing them back; runs the 29 steps (publication, started-word-is-0 check, the vendor register sequence with every 64-bit register as two 32-bit accesses, a wait of at most 1 s for the 32-bit started word, yielding one scheduler tick after each 50 µs of reads); reports the controller result, started word, marker and start timestamp, system data flags and power state, connection states, executed command count, and read-backs of SOFT_RESET and the eleven MIPS wrapper registers. The image leaves the GPU powered with the firmware running and the lifetime ends with a power removal; the vendor stops the firmware only after the firmware's own forced-idle and power-off handshake, which this image has no command queue or interrupt service for. The firmware's MIPS page table maps only the image's own firmware and shared pages. Every GPU, wrapper and SMC0 access is one 32-bit access made after the progress record names it and after a GPU FWS reading or writing log line.

The timer record adds two 32-bit reads (four after a low-word wrap) and one 40-byte write; the secure configuration adds two writes and two observation reads; splitting the fourteen 64-bit register writes and four 64-bit reads into 32-bit halves adds 18 accesses to its 24. The log of a complete run in the host check is 8,047 bytes of the 16,128-byte log area. checks/pvr-gpu-start.c and checks/pvr-gpu-start-reference.py cover the 29-step controller: 36 retained faults, 40 refusals and the reference traces less SOFT_RESET2 (~/.cache/sunstoneos/evidence/gpu-start-20261025/). apps/gpu-power-id/check.py --fw-start runs eleven cases on the linked image with only the ON, the clock, translations, cache maintenance and the log modeled: the complete start (CR timer read once and, after a low-word wrap, twice); a start that times out, finds the started word already set, or reads 2; a CORE6 that does not reach 8, an unexpected identity, a wrong SMC0 mapping, a write-back translation of a shared page, a start refused by the deadlines; and a seeded mutant of the SMC0 write value.
